df888992ccfc74ac380a2a5114596095415769fc.summary: Malpedia family page for Kazuar, a backdoor linked to the Turla actor. It has no description of its own. Its references run from 2017 to 2026 and come from Unit 42, Microsoft, Kaspersky, Accenture, CERT-UA, Google and others. The references name Turla, Secret Blizzard and Pensive Ursa as related actors, and list CAPIBAR, HyperStack and Carbon as companion tools.

df8c6e17acdd0d83a9127877a405b9425a1e5fd2.summary: CSIS management report on the threat landscape in H1 2019, written by the CSIS security group. It covers Emotet and Trickbot botnets, Magecart web-skimming growth, GrandGrab and other ransomware (including an incident at a hosting company), banking trojans such as Ramnit, TomcatBanker and Anubis, cash-out and package mule fraud, PayPal phishing and smishing, and APT activity attributed to Lazarus, Empire Monkey, FIN7 and BARIUM. Much of the data is statistics cited from other vendors. The report is commercial and includes CSIS product updates.

hedges: CSIS believed it was written by a fairly skilled developer.
According to CSIS sources, the group involved was Empire Monkey.
Attribution of the BARIUM group points towards it, according to Kaspersky investigations.
Investigators believed the intruders were using ScreenConnect on hacked Wipro systems to reach client systems.
CSIS suspected the initial information gathering could be used to segment victims before a second stage payload.
Not much substantive news regarding the Carbanak leak itself was found.
CSIS had not yet confirmed any Asacub variants in the wild.
Dark forum chatter suggested an Emotet resurgence was planned for H2 2019, though the infrastructure went silent in June.
